subject: Doorway criteria, exit checks & validation runbook (MAP)
messages:
From: Raj Patel <raj@medalign.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Ellen Cho <ellen@medalign.com>
Date: 2026-08-29T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff – what counts as 'done' for our evaluation?

Vivek / team,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. As we move into the 4-week evaluation window, our execs want a tight definition of what success looks like — not just uptime and latency, but concrete exit checks we can sign off on.

High-level asks from MedAlign:
- A shortlist of pass/fail checks we can put in our procurement checklist (regulatory, performance, data handling).
- One-page runbook for smoke/integration tests our engineers can run during the trial.
- Clear owners and timeline so we can bind internal approval to dates.

Can you share a proposed "doorway" set of criteria (i.e., the minimal bar to move into pilot-to-prod negotiations) and the sample tests you expect us to run? Preferably by end-of-week so we can review with security.

—Raj
Senior Product Manager
MedAlign Health

Attachments: none
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>

Cc: Ellen Cho <ellen@medalign.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff – what counts as 'done' for our evaluation?

Raj, Ellen — good framing. Attaching a draft checklist (doorway-criteria-checklist.xlsx) and a short smoke-test spec (smoke-test-cases.md). Below is a compact doorway proposal we think maps cleanly to your procurement review.

Doorway criteria (minimal bar to move from evaluation -> procurement/negotiation):
1) Security & Data Controls (non-negotiable)
   - SOC2 scope confirmation: Redwood will provide latest attestation and evidence for ingestion controls.
   - Data residency guarantee for PII samples used in the trial (logs retained < 30 days).
2) Deterministic smoke performance
   - 99th percentile response latency <= 250ms for 1–4 token prompt baseline on dedicated-tiny model.
   - End-to-end throughput of 50 QPS sustained for 10m with <1% error rate in our test harness.
3) Functional correctness (quality check)
   - Task-level precision: regression against your golden set >= 92% (we'll exchange the golden set).
   - No high-severity hallucination failures in 200 sampled prompts (failure defined in attached spec).
4) Operational observability
   - Token-level cost and latency traces visible in console for the trial environment.
   - Exportable audit log for 7 days (with vendor-provided proof-of-delivery).
5) Integration & rollback
   - Example integration with your staging environment via API key rotation and per-route model pinning.
   - Clear rollback trigger: if >3 production-impacting errors in 24h during pilot, auto-fallback to model variant.

Proposed owners & run schedule:
- Redwood: provide checklist, test vectors, and a step-by-step smoke test runner (deliver by Thu). (Owner: Marissa Cole)
- MedAlign: run the smoke script against staging and return results + 10 failure examples (Owner: Raj).
- Success decision: joint review call on Week 2 Monday; if doorway criteria met, move to procurement packet.

I attached the checklist and the smoke-test cases. Happy to iterate — if you want, Marissa can walk through the checklist tomorrow.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Partnerships & GTM
Redwood Inference

Attachments: doorway-criteria-checklist.xlsx, smoke-test-cases.md
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-08-31T14:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff – what counts as 'done' for our evaluation?

Looping Ben in to confirm the test harness and to outline the quick-fix plan for any performance gaps. Ben — if we see latency slip at 99th during the queueing test, our playbook is: 1) enable prefix KV caching for matched routes, 2) bump to a quantization-safe variant, 3) if still bad, advise a short burst (10m) on Dedicated capacity.

A couple of notes on the checklist we've attached (high-level):
- Evidence required: for each security item, list the exact artifact (SOC2 PDF, control owner, timestamp).
- For the golden set quality test, MedAlign should provide the canonical ground truth (we will not share internal prompts).
- Smoke runner: a single script that returns pass/fail per-case plus an artifacts bundle (logs + tokens) that MedAlign can upload to the Drive link.

Proposed timeline:
- Thu (2026-09-02): Redwood delivers test runner and postman collection.
- Fri (2026-09-03): MedAlign runs tests & returns results.
- Mon (2026-09-06): Joint decision call; if doorway satisfied, prepare procurement packet by 9/10.

Ben — can you confirm you can deliver the runner by Thu?

—Marissa
Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference

- Default test set: 200 prompts (150 quality probes, 30 stress latency, 20 edge/regulatory probes).
- Pass thresholds: overall pass >= 90% on quality probes AND 99p latency <= 250ms on the stress set.
